claims.text: Incorporating a nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloy system into an as-fabricated W-Cu metal-matrix composite will increase its thermal conductivity.
Incorporating the nanocrystalline RHEA system will retain the mechanical durability of the W-Cu composite.
Incorporating the nanocrystalline RHEA system will retain the irradiation resistance of the W-Cu composite.
The intervention produces or introduces a nanocrystalline grain structure in the modified W-Cu composite.
The intervention introduces a high-entropy alloy composition into the modified W-Cu composite.
The nanocrystalline RHEA optimizes grain-boundary scattering in a way that enhances thermal conductivity.
The nanocrystalline RHEA enhances phonon transport in the W-Cu composite.
The inherent properties of RHEAs preserve mechanical durability under the stated application conditions.
The inherent properties of RHEAs preserve irradiation resistance under the stated application conditions.
The predicted thermal-conductivity increase is relative to an otherwise comparable W-Cu composite without the nanocrystalline RHEA.
The modified composite will show no significant degradation in mechanical durability relative to the comparator.
The modified composite will show no significant degradation in irradiation resistance relative to the comparator.
The hypothesis is intended to hold at high temperature and high radiation flux representative of heat-dissipation and fusion-reactor joint applications.
Interactions between the RHEA and the W-Cu phases may affect performance.
Failure to obtain a significant thermal-conductivity increase, or observation of significant degradation in mechanical durability or irradiation resistance, would falsify the hypothesis.
